summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted electively for cardiac catheterization due to increased frequency of chest discomfort and new left ventricular wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram. He was heparin-brided off warfarin and underwent cardiac catheterization, which showed stable coronary artery disease with patent stents and no new interventions required. His warfarin was restarted and adjusted to 4 mg daily with an INR of 2.5 at discharge. Heart failure was managed medically with no acute decompensation. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, follow up with cardiology, and check INR as scheduled.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Heart valve replaced by other means
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
